title: GPS-LOGELASTIC: wider combiners reduce source copies at the same full time envelope

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), the ONE GPS-LOGELASTIC program in proof.md with fixed selected beta=1/8,eta=1,gamma=-15/16 recovers the whole secret from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. For n<2^4096 it runs the explicit exhaustive finite branch; otherwise v=ceil(sqrt n), ell=ceil(log2n), h=ceil(ell^(1/8)), b=v*(ell+2h-16), m=ceil((n-1)/b), with top-down widths, positive r_i=b_i+1 and unit zero-width shortcuts. All source/decoder/precision and acquisition/fallback quantities are recomputed. On EVERY branch, including failed work, discarded copies, wrong labels and both aborts, paid time T is O(2^((1/2)sqrt(n)*log2n+sqrt(n)*(log2n)^(1/8))) with exact growth index1/2. Outside constants are absolute independent of N,s and outcomes. All source, arithmetic, circuit generation, initialization, reset, measurement, preprocessing, full addressing and cleanup costs are paid jointly with all other resources and clean fraction0 for this same configuration.

For the same GPS-LOGELASTIC algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
